locator.section: Feria II post dominicam I Passionis, Postcommunio (Sacramenti tui); seventeen-word conclusion prefix

entries.claim: The accented printed example has seventeen words through Deus, ending with a full stop. It supports no comma after Christum, tuum: Qui and Sancti, Deus. It does not print the final four words per omnia saecula saeculorum or Amen at this locus.

The unaccented rubric prints the ordinary Father-directed conclusion: twenty-one Latin words followed by Amen. It supplies the lexical expansion of the proper page's Per Dominum cue; it prints tuum, qui rather than the selected accented prefix's tuum: Qui.

The cited proper page prints the 26-word prayer body and its abbreviated Per Dóminum cue. The selected standalone long conclusion and response are supplied by the separately declared shared formula, variant-rule and printed-prefix sources.

locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

These rules prescribe the different conclusions for references or addresses to the Son, mention of the Holy Spirit, and specially printed endings. This prayer's body addresses the Father without mentioning the Son or Holy Spirit, so the ordinary conclusion applies.
